title: Charge-anchor protocol: client-side seals and server arbitration for retry-safe billing
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem:
Customers have reported overcharges when clients perform retries after receiving partial responses (HTTP 202 chunked generation, WebSocket disconnects, or network blips). Current ingest paths are at-least-once and rely on client-generated dedupe fingerprints or aggressive lease windows which either push complexity to SDKs or lead to edge corner-cases where duplicates slip through.

Goal:
Design and ship a lightweight server-backed "charge-anchor" protocol: clients attach an opaque client-seal with each request attempt; the server issues a short-lived commit marker (charge-anchor) when it is safe to bill a completed response. On retries the server will arbitrate based on seals and anchors to ensure exactly-once charge semantics (or bounded partial-charge reconciliation) without forcing strong client-side coordination.

Non-goals:
- Replace long-term consumption ledger or accounting services.
- Eliminate all user-visible duplicate tokens for historical sessions older than the anchor TTL.

Constraints:
- Must work across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments (no centrally-hosted unique-ids required).
- Minimal extra latency on the hot path (<= 2ms at edge for anchor validation).
- Graceful fallback when cross-region RPCs for arbitration time out: safe conservative billing (favor crediting rather than double-charging).

High-level approach:
1) Client generates a random client-seal per logical request attempt and sends it in X-Client-Seal header. SDKs will provide this by default.
2) Server accepts attempts and attaches an internal provisional token for ongoing generation. If a response completes, the serving node writes a charge-anchor to a short-lived anchor store (region-local lease, TTL 5m) containing {seal, model-version, outcome-hash, token-count, completion-ts}.
3) On receiving duplicate attempts with the same or different seals, the serving layer consults the anchor store and applies arbitration rules to decide: reuse anchor (no extra charge), merge partial outputs and attribute incremental tokens (partial-charge arbitration), or treat as new charge if anchor absent/expired.
4) Anchors are replicated to a reconciliation queue for the consumption ledger to absorb final credits. A reconciliation pass is responsible for converting anchors into final invoices and emitting corrections if partial-charge arbitration applied.

Design trade-offs considered:
- Strong globally unique nonces vs regional seals: picked region-local seals to avoid cross-region latency spikes and to support private deployments.
- Synchronous anchor writes vs async best-effort: initial design uses synchronous local anchor write (fast local store) to avoid race windows; we fall back to async write for overloaded edge nodes with compensating reconciliation heuristics.
- Conservative crediting on uncertainty vs optimistic: choose conservative (credit back) to protect customers and revenue trust.

Acceptance criteria:
- SDKs emit client-seal header by default for all text/generation APIs.
- No verified cases of double-charge for retries in a 30-day canary across 50 customers using heavy retry patterns (simulated failures).
- Anchor write adds <2ms median latency at p50 and <10ms p99 on our staging infra.
- Reconciliation job can process anchors at current peak throughput with <5m catch-up time on restart.
- End-to-end e2e test covering partial-response restart and merge passes in CI.

Rollout plan:
Phase 1 (canary): Edge-only, hosted API, 5% of traffic, read-only validation (anchors written and logged but not used for arbitration).
Phase 2: Canary arbitration on a small customer cohort with opt-in flag; monitor double-charge alerts, billing diffs, and anchor store health.
Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 100% across hosted, then Dedicated; issue optional private deployment adapter for on-prem anchor store (local DB).

Metrics to monitor:
- duplicate_charge_alerts: number of detected double-charge incidents per hour.
- anchor_write_latency_ms: histogram.
- arbitration_decisions: counts by decision type (reuse, merge, new_charge, uncertain_fallback).
- reconciliation_lag_seconds: delay between anchor write and ledger finalization.
- customer_billing_delta: difference in billed tokens before/after arbitration.

Open questions / risks:
- How to attrib partial-token merges deterministically across two independent attempts that each returned partial outputs? (Proposed: outcome-hash + token-count merge heuristics, tie-breaker by earliest completion-ts.)
- Edge anchor store durability guarantees in private/on-prem environments: need a minimal local DB adapter and docs for operators.
- Attack vector: malicious client reuse of seals to attempt free replays. Mitigation: short TTLs, client identity binding (API key), and rate limits per key + per-seal heuristics.

- Proto spec and state machine: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folder/charge-anchor-spec
